report.headline: Usage projected to fall from 24.9% in the EuroLeague to 19.5% in the NBA, landing near the league-average 20.1%, while the true shooting projection carries no信息 because the model loses to a trivial baseline on that metric.

projection.text: The model projects a 19.5% usage rate in the NBA, down from 24.9% in the source EuroLeague season, essentially matching the target league's minutes-weighted average of 20.1%.

risks.text: Projected usage of 19.5% represents a real drop from the 24.9% share carried in the EuroLeague, and lands almost exactly at the NBA average rather than above it, meaning a reduced offensive role is the central expectation, not a tail case.

The true shooting projection of 57.9% cannot be relied upon: the model's 4.5% error is worse than the 4.3% error of simply predicting the league mean, so any efficiency number quoted here — including the wide 95% band of 48.9% to 67.0% — should be treated as uninformative rather than a real forecast.

The estimate rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, and the player was already only modestly above his own league's average entering the move (+0.46 sd), a smaller starting edge than his measured usage (+0.92 sd) or shooting (+1.01 sd) standing might suggest.
At age 27 in the source season, the projection is drawn from a model fit on movers broadly and carries no separate adjustment for his specific age.

strengths.text: Scored at a 21.6 points-per-75-possessions clip in the source season.
Posted a source-season true shooting percentage of 65.3%, +1.01 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average that year.
Rebounded at 8.4 per 75 possessions while drawing 42.9% of shot attempts from three, indicating a floor-spacing, glass-crashing profile.
Kept turnovers low at a 6.9% turnover rate despite a heavy 24.9% usage rate and shot volume in the EuroLeague.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 13.9% to 25.0%, an 11.1-point spread against a league standard deviation of 5.6%, so the model can rank this player's likely role but cannot pin a single number; the true shooting projection of 57.9% should not be trusted at all, since the model's held-out error (4.5%) is worse than simply guessing the league mean (4.3%).
